signal: KlariVis now serves over 130 financial institutions across 35 states and recently added b1Bank as a customer on its core-agnostic analytics platform.

email.body1:
Amber, saw KlariVis crossed 130 financial institutions across 35 states and recently added b1Bank to the platform.

Growth like that usually means more community banks and credit unions in play than your team can work before they go quiet. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up on its own, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a signal play for KlariVis off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Amber, quick follow-up for KlariVis.

As you scale past 130 institutions, expectations on pipeline tend to jump faster than headcount can. Most teams do not actually know how many meetings they need to hit the number, so the gap shows up late and the quarter becomes a scramble.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I will walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings KlariVis needs to hit target, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Amber, last bit of proof for KlariVis.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and could not hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email logged to CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how your reply rate likely compares to other banking-tech teams. Want to hop on a quick call so I can walk you through it?
email.body4:
Amber, I will stop reaching out on this one, but did not want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling pipeline without adding headcount is not a priority this quarter, no problem at all. Running both sales and marketing is its own kind of busy.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to a banking-tech motion? I will tailor it to KlariVis either way.
